surprises.description: R&D Solutions generated $3.2B of net new bookings, above the preview’s implied $3.0–3.1B, while LTM bookings rose to $11.7B and advanced for a fifth consecutive quarter. The preview expected about $11.3B of LTM bookings and four consecutive quarters of increases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D Solutions delivered $3.2 billion in net new bookings, up 15% year-over-year for the strongest clinical bookings in four years”; “Last-12-month net new bookings reached $11.7 billion, up 14% year-over-year and rising for five consecutive quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “net new bookings of roughly $3.0–3.1B”; “LTM bookings $11.3B (+13%) have risen four straight quarters.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $4.428B beat the $4.37B consensus, and organic growth was approximately 6%, above the high end of guidance. The reported 8% growth also exceeded the preview’s expected 6.4% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue reached $4.428 billion, growing 8% reported and 8.6% at constant currency, with organic growth of approximately 6%—more than 2x the prior-year rate and above the high end of guidance.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $3.34 beat the preview’s $3.24–$3.25 consensus range and its $3.30–$3.32 working whisper estimate. Growth of 11.3% was also ahead of the preview’s expected 8.0% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS rose 11.3% to $3.34, beating guidance driven entirely by operational performance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $3.24–$3.25 ... YoY +8.0%”; “a functional whisper of roughly $3.30–3.32 is a reasonable working assumption.”

surprises.description: IQVIA raised its full-year 2026 guidance rather than merely narrowing it to the upper half as the preview expected. The increase was modest, however: the new EPS range still tops out at $13.00, below the preview’s bull-case threshold of raising above $13.05.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance: revenue to $17.35–$17.50 billion, adjusted EBITDA to $4.025–$4.055 billion, and adjusted EPS to $12.90–$13.00.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Narrowing to the upper half ($17.40–17.48B / $12.95–13.05) is the base case”; the bull scenario called for “FY EPS raised above $13.05.”

surprises.description: A review of inactive trials cut contracted backlog by about $2.1B, leaving it at $32.6B versus the $34.67B consensus figure. The preview had flagged inactive trials as a backlog-quality risk, but the size of the reduction was still a material headline shortfall; stronger near-term backlog revenue partly offsets that concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A detailed review of inactive trials led to a ~$2.1 billion backlog reduction, with contracted backlog ending at $32.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Contracted backlog | $34.67B”; the preview also noted “~5% of backlog could be inactive trials” and that management said it “wouldn't affect guidance.”

surprises.description: Revenue expected from backlog over the next 12 months rose to $9.4B, up 10%, ahead of the preview’s $9.2B and 7.5% growth reading. That is stronger near-term backlog conversion than the preview’s 8%+ acceleration target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “next-12-months revenue from backlog at $9.4 billion, up 10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$9.2B at June 30, +7.5% YoY”; “It needs to hold ≥7.5% and ideally accelerate toward 8%+.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was slightly above the preview’s estimate, and margin expanded 20 basis points for a second straight quarter despite an approximately 60-basis-point net non-operational headwind. Excluding pass-through and currency effects, underlying margin improvement was about 80 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $1.032 billion (up 8.7%) with 20 basis points of margin expansion, the second consecutive quarter of expansion despite an ~60 bps net non-operational headwind”; “underlying adjusted EBITDA margins would have improved approximately 80 basis points.”

surprises.description: Broader demand indicators were notably strong: EBP funding reached $90B year-to-date, while clinical trial starts and RFP flow were up high single digits and new drug launches were up over 40%. This extended beyond the preview’s more general account of a funding recovery and its watch for improved RFP volumes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EBP funding up more than 85% year-to-date to $90 billion, clinical trial starts up high single digits, RFP flow up high single digits, and new drug launches up over 40%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “biotech funding has rebounded past ~$50B year-to-date”; the preview’s bull commentary included “RFP volumes up.”

surprises.description: Net leverage ended at 3.45x, below the 3.59x level cited in the preview, indicating a stronger balance-sheet position than that reference point. The preview flagged leverage and capital discipline as watch items.
surprises.fact_evidence: “net leverage ended at 3.45x trailing-12-month adjusted EBITDA.”
